notes: Catch region is EXACTLY as described — the try/catch boundary is unmoved; only _psmDonate's contents widened, by exactly the three reverts the story enumerates.

Silent USDS parking on unset/unregistered streamer IS acknowledged by the story and the NatSpec, with recovery and monitoring guidance. The dust branch's loss of DonationSkipped is NOT acknowledged — see F-01-047.

findings.specText: DonationSkipped NatSpec: "Emitted when a donation attempt is silently skipped (PSM outage / fee spike / dust). `usdsParked` USDS stays on the contract for the next dispatch to retry." — alongside the same commit's new ops note: "This means a streamer misconfiguration is quiet: watch `DonationSkipped` and the contract's USDS balance."
findings.specSource: src/dispatchers/BalancerPoolerV2.sol NatSpec (event decl. line 134) + git commit d4cc563 body
findings.actualBehavior: Replacing require(gemAmt > 0) with if (gemAmt > 0) makes _psmDonate return normally on a dust sweep, so no event is emitted at all — neither DonationSkipped nor BatchDonatedViaPSM. Under e4de393 the same condition reverted into the caller's catch and emitted DonationSkipped(remainingUSDS).
findings.deviation: The code change is authorised by story-047 bullet 4, but the contract's own documented observability contract still lists dust as a DonationSkipped trigger, and the same commit instructs operators to monitor that event. Dust-driven skips became invisible in logs and no story or NatSpec line acknowledges it.
findings.impact: Monitoring-fidelity only. Requires gemAmt to floor to zero (sub-1e-6-USDC sweep); the USDS parks and is re-swept, so no value is at risk.
findings.recommendation: Emit DonationSkipped(usdsAmount) in the else branch of the guard, or strike 'dust' from the event NatSpec and note it in the contract-level ops block.

findings.specText: story-046 NatSpec: "If the streamer is set but ops forgot registerStream(batchMinter, _token, duration) on it, every dispatch reverts NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered(). This is the accepted consequence of the mandatory-streamer decision, NOT an audit finding. … Repointing batchMinter to an address with no registered stream re-arms the same failure mode; register the new pair first."
findings.specSource: git commit 1745e83 body + src/dispatchers/NudgeRatchet.sol contract NatSpec
findings.actualBehavior: NFTMinterV2._executeMint (src/NFTMinterV2.sol:191) calls dispatch with no try/catch, so NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered()/"nudgeStreamer unset" bubbles out and every user mint at that dispatcher index reverts. NudgeRatchet has no donation-disable switch, so the brick is total once it holds any balance.
findings.deviation: The story's blanket 'NOT an audit finding' declaration is over-broad. It is correct for the deploy-ordering case (fails loudly on the first dispatch, obvious to any competent operator — Law 3 suppress). It is NOT correct for the repoint case: setBatchMinter/setRecipient on a LIVE dispatcher succeeds silently and arms the revert on every subsequent user mint, and clearing it requires an onlyOwner call on NudgeStreamer in a different repository (phoenix-nft-staking) plus a whitelist call on the batch-minter. No view or guard on the dispatcher surfaces the missing registration. A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised — Law-3 footgun, in scope.
findings.law1Assessment: No escalation. No value at risk: the user's payment transferFrom occurs inside the same reverting transaction (NFTMinterV2.sol:183), so nothing is stranded and no NFT is minted against a lost payment. Availability-only, owner-recoverable via NFTMinterV2 config.disabled or via registerStream.
findings.recommendation: Probe INudgeStreamer(nudgeStreamer).pendingStream(newSink, token) inside setBatchMinter/setRecipient as a cheap registration signal, or bind the sink repoint to the registerStream call in the ops runbook.

findings.specText: NudgeStreamer contract NatSpec (the purpose stories 046/047 import): "Buffers bursty donations per (batchMinter, token) and streams them linearly to zero over a configured duration, so that whoever calls batchMint right after a burst can no longer capture a disproportionate share of the reward pot."
findings.actualBehavior: release(amount) still does IERC20(_token).safeTransfer(batchMinter, amount) — a lump payment straight to the sink, bypassing the streamer. All four other donors into the same sink are now metered; this fifth one is not.
findings.deviation: No literal deviation from story text — story-046 scopes itself to three named dispatchers and story-047 to BalancerPoolerV2; neither mentions NudgeRatchetDelayRelease. Recorded as a coverage gap because the imported goal is only partially achieved: a mempool-visible release(X) remains front-/back-runnable by a batchMint caller, exactly the burst-capture the streamer exists to prevent.
findings.impact: Low. release is onlyReleaser, so burst timing is admin-chosen not attacker-chosen, and the contract is itself a manual rate-control throttle by design. Residual is the single-block capture window around each release tx.
findings.dedupNote: Same MEV class as phoenix-nft-staking ledger entry 858e9e80 (nudge front-running, wont-fix), but a different contract in a different repo — do NOT collapse into it.
findings.recommendation: Either route release() through collectNudge (same shape as NudgeRatchet), or add a NatSpec line stating the omission is deliberate because the contract already provides admin rate control.
